name: Sulista/Gaúcho Portuguese
notes: Sulista / Gaúcho (Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul). Strong /r/ is the velar fricative [x]: in Porto Alegre the trill fell 'de 30,9% nos anos 1990 para apenas 0,4%' (Corrêa 2020: 87), and ALiB shows 'o predomínio do uso da fricativa velar [x] nos estados do Rio Grande do Sul e Santa Catarina' (Comiotto & Margotti 2019: PDF p. 6); the trill survives at Italian-contact points. /t d/ affricate before [i]: ALiB rates Porto Alegre categorical (Battisti & Dornelles Filho 2015: 226). Final /o/ raises in 97 % of Porto Alegre tokens (Franceschini & Loregian-Penkal 2023: 2), and no opened source gives final [e] retention for the capital, so final vowels follow the base. Coda /R/ is the tap, 'from São Paulo southwards' (Barbosa & Albano 2004: 228).

allophone_rules.notes: A coda /S/ takes the voicing of a following voiced consonant: mesmo [ˈmezmu], desde [ˈdezd͡ʒi]. Barbosa & Albano (2004: 229): 'it tends to assimilate the voicing of the following sound'. The list leaves out the tap and reads the next slot on the second pass, after BR_STRONG_R_AFTER_CODA has written ⟨r⟩ as the voiceless strong rhotic [x], so a coda sibilant before it stays voiceless: desrespeito [desxesˈpejtu].

An ⟨r⟩ after a coda consonant is the strong rhotic of rato [ˈxatu] and carro [ˈkaxu]: honra [ˈõxɐ], genro [ˈʒẽxu]. Cristófaro Silva (2025: 240) puts the R-forte in one class across three contexts: 'início de sílaba que coincide com início de palavra (rapaz, rio, rosa etc.); início de sílaba em meio de palavra (carro, terra) ou início de sílaba após consoante (Israel, desrespeito etc.)'.
